page: Microsoft Azure F64alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine within the Faldsv7 family, built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio, totaling 64 vCPUs. The processor cache consists of 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, complemented by support for advanced vector and matrix instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory is configured at 128.0 GB, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Memory throughput reaches 415.58 GB/sec for uncached read-only large blocks and 205.55 GB/sec for write operations, with cached small-block reads delivering 11887.44 GB/sec. Local storage comprises 7559 GB of high-speed NVMe SSD capacity. The server does not include discrete GPU hardware accelerators and is provisioned without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark outcomes place the F64alds_v7 in the top tier (top 10%) across compute and compilation tasks, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 31093.0, a Clang compilation score of 85650.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 115141.66. Compression and decompression tests reflect exceptional throughput, demonstrated by 870.96 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 40.81 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. In web and caching workloads, it processes 166.56 million Redis SET operations per second and handles 96.82 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The 2.0 GB per core memory footprint represents a deliberate design tradeoff, prioritizing dense computational throughput and high clock speeds over large in-memory capacities. This configuration delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound workloads requiring substantial fast local NVMe scratch storage, such as Clang/code compilation pipelines, batch analytics, physics simulations, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure F64alds_v7 is a compute-optimized instance driven by a 64-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping. Delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs, 128.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU), and a bundled 7559 GB NVMe SSD local drive, the instance achieves top-tier results in CPU and memory benchmarks. It supports instruction sets such as AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and VAES. Benchmark performance highlights include a Geekbench multi-core score of 31093.0, Clang software compilation throughput of 85650.0, and 166.56 million Redis SET operations per second. With no discrete GPUs and a lean memory-to-core ratio, it offers high efficiency for large-scale software builds, CPU-based machine learning inference, continuous integration pipelines, and intensive batch computing requiring low-latency local storage.
